To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the limiting power of autocorrelation tests in regression models with restricted coefficients can be zero even when there is an intercept term, but is always strictly greater than zero when the restrictions are valid.

the limiting power of the Durbin-Wa ton test can drop to zero even when an intercept is included in a regression model with linear restrictions on coefficients and that for a regression with valid restrictions the Durbin-Waston statistic has the same limiting distribution as that of an equivalent regression without restrictions.

1) the Durbin-Wats on and other tests for first- order autocorrelation have a zero limit in the unrestricted model with no intercept and in the restricted model with a zero intercept; 2) the limit of these tests is a constant lying strictly be tween zero and one when the intercept is nonzero and the restrictions are valid; 3) the limit of the Durbin-Wa tson and related statistics is the same in the restricted and unrestricted model if the restrictions are valid
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general class of tests for linear restrictions in a linear regression.
the limiting power of the Durbin-Wu test in the presence of linear restrictions, and with the algebraic forms of the Durbin- Watson statistic under restrictions.
the limiting power of the Durbin-Wa tson and related tests for first-order serial correlation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the limiting power of the Durbin-Wu atson statistic and several other tests of first-order autocorrelat ion in a regression model with linear restrictions on some of the coefficients is equal to one if the model is valid.

the Durbin -Watson test and several other tests have limiting power zero in the unrestricted regression, limiting power one in the restricted regression without an intercept, but a power lying strictly between these limits when an intercept is present.

the limiting power of the tests for first-order serial correlation in regression models is not affected by the presence of linear restrictions on the parameters, except when the restrictions are not valid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Durbin- Watson test and the Breusch- Godfrey test for first-order autocorr elation have limiting power of zero in the restricted model with an intercept term.
the power of the Durbin-Watsom test is not affected by the linear restrictions, but the power of the other tests is reduced.

in the linear regression models with restricted coefficients and linear restrictions, the Durbin-Wu atson and several other autocorrelation tests have limiting power of zero, one or a constant strictly between these values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the Durbin-Wa ton test, the inclusion of an inter cept in a regression with linear restrictions does not guarantee a positive limiting power.
the limiting power of autocorrelation tests is not a reliable indicator of the performance of these tests in restricted regression models.
, in the presence of restrictions on the parameters, the limiting power of autocorrelation tests can still be zero even with the addition of an intercept term.
